authors: ML dataset ordinary binary root and BSGS pilot

claims.text: Exactly 16 frozen plan indices have one retained native generate attempt each, including censored and failed outcomes.
Where a root cell completes, its binary S3 distinct-root and group-lift certificates pass the native independent verifier; root evidence is PDP evidence and is not an ECDLP scalar-recovery label.
A BSGS cell is labelled solved ECDLP only when its independently recovered scalar and known-answer identity pass native verify for the corresponding public generator and target.
Each completed shard has its native report, strict public/restricted export, restricted archive and fresh S3 byte-equality receipt; failures at every stage remain counted.
No root-versus-BSGS speed, whole-worker instruction, exact fall-degree, ECDLP advantage or broader matrix claim is inferred from this pilot.

aa.not_applicable_reason: Absolute software coverage, replay and custody; no comparative performance claim or timing-effect inference.

negative.not_applicable_reason: Exact accounting of the fixed selected population; no detector false-positive or null-population inference.

positive.not_applicable_reason: Each BSGS solved claim requires independent group replay; each completed root certificate has native mathematical replay. No sensitivity claim is made.

decision_rule.interval: Not applicable: exact fixed-population accounting without inferential interval
decision_rule.statistic: Exact counts by solver, twist and terminal outcome; native root-certificate replay, independently recovered ECDLP cells and S3 readback-complete cells
decision_rule.text: Count all 16 planned indices and outcomes. Promote a root certificate only after native replay, and an ECDLP solve only after independently recovered BSGS scalar plus native verify. Custody requires restricted S3 archive PUT and fresh GET byte comparison. Retain failures, timeouts and missing stages.

inadmissible: replacing a seed or shard after failure
dropping failed, timed-out or interrupted attempts
calling a recorded known-answer scalar an independently recovered ECDLP without native verify
using restricted witness material as public ML features
promoting missing S3 readback as durable
claiming storage or solver speedup from unmatched runs
calling a root certificate an ECDLP scalar solve
comparing root and BSGS wall times as a performance claim
promoting an incomplete root call to a negative PDP result
invalidation_rules: Binary, plan or protocol file digest changes invalidate new admission.
Existing marker or live worker blocks a new attempt for that shard.
A missing or failed independent native verify prevents solution promotion.
A missing fresh S3 GET or hash mismatch prevents durability promotion.
A root artifact cannot provide an ECDLP label, even if a matched BSGS cell solves the public instance.

question: Can all 16 frozen ordinary binary n23 m2 root and BSGS cells across paired twists, generators and keys retain exact terminal outcomes, replay applicable native certificates, and preserve restricted S3 custody?

instance_sampling.rule: Four shared instance IDs g0k0, g0k1, g1k0, g1k1 in every solver-by-twist arm. Root and BSGS share exact public input within a twist; opposite twists are distinct curves. Entire fixed16-cell plan retained without outcome selection.

seed_derivation.note: Native plan seed20261031 fixed before data; curve seed index0.

power.note: Four instance IDs per arm (generator0/1 by key0/1), four solver-by-twist arms, exactly16 native cells; no inferential effect or power claim.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Per-arm planning allowance of 4*80s plus 20s admission. Four arms imply up to 1360s for 16 cells; each generate has a 90s outer cap. This is an allowance, not a binary-root runtime estimate or performance claim.

stopping_rules.rule: All 16 plan indices0..15, one new solver attempt each; retain every outcome and no replacement.

Each generate has 30s inner and90s outer cap; each verify/report/export/archive/PUT/GET stage has a finite controller cap. Stop on failed custody and resume finalization only; at least4GiB XFS free before each new attempt.
